sections.overview: Thomisus onustus is a flower-dwelling crab spider found across much of Europe, North Africa and Asia.
sections.identification: Females are much larger than males and may be white, yellow or pink; their colour can change over several days.
sections.habitat: It waits on flowers, especially in warm, sunny sites, where flower visitors come within reach.
sections.diet: It ambushes visiting insects, including bees, butterflies and hoverflies.
sections.behavior: Its flower-coloured appearance offers imperfect camouflage, and how conspicuous it is can affect its risk of attack.
sections.reproduction: The consulted identification and field sources do not provide a sufficiently detailed account of its reproduction.
sections.ecology: By ambushing pollinating insects, it is a predator within flower-visiting insect communities.
sections.conservation: The consulted sources provide a broad range but no global conservation assessment.
